lessons: A super-crazy move in one asset class spills into all other asset classes.

summary: Budget-day aftermath: STT hike (options ~0.1%→0.15%) sank the market, but the budget otherwise contained positives — TCS (remittance) cut 20%→2% with threshold ₹7L→₹10L, FPI stake cap 5%→10%, GST waived on FPI brokerage. Detailed FPI economics: STT per crore of premium turnover rises ₹5,000 vs ₹300 GST saved. Sellers will pass costs to buyers via premiums. ITM put-calendar max loss quantified (70-80 points). BSE/MCX fell 10%+ in the knee-jerk. Nifty closed below the May-12 ceasefire level (~24,925) first time in ~9 months; 16-month return about -6%.

events.claim: Union Budget (presented 1 Feb 2026) raised securities transaction tax on options from ~0.1% to ~0.15% of premium
Budget 2026 cut Tax Collected at Source on remittances from 20% to 2% and raised the threshold from ₹7 lakh to ₹10 lakh

lessons: Option sellers pass tax costs to buyers; premiums inflate to absorb STT hikes.
One negative headline can erase a broadly positive budget — markets trade the disappointment, not the document.
Think like a businessman outside the market: diagnose and adjust instead of clinging to a stop-loss.

summary: 'Operation successful, patient dead': the speaker's heavy pre-budget bullish position was unwound at a loss when the STT hike hit — then the India-US trade deal arrived two days later (tariff 50%→25%→18%), triggering GIFT Nifty +800 (~3%). South Korea swung -5%→+5% in two days. Core lessons: buy near hedges not far ones (₹2-3 25,600CE caps loss 300 points away), expect black swans on the upside too, and the May-12 pattern (1,000-point spike then 6-month consolidation).

events.claim: India-US trade deal announced 3 Feb 2026: US tariffs on India cut from 50% to 25% and reportedly to 18%
GIFT Nifty indicated ~800-point (~3%) gap-up on the trade-deal news

lessons: Buy hedges near, not far: a ₹3 hedge caps loss 300 points away; skipping it costs 700.

Disaster strikes when you least expect it; the May-12 pattern says monster moves consolidate for months.
